rules.sentence: A regular, round-shaped lesion with high internal reflectivity and moderate attenuation of echoes is characteristic of CVM.

On computed tomography scan, CVM appears as a well-circumscribed, hyperdense, homogenous, intraconal lesion, seen as a discrete mass that does not directly adhere to the extra-ocular muscles and optic nerve and may occasionally erode the bone.
Phleboliths, which are pathognomonic of venous malformations and are caused by chronic inflammation in long-standing cases, may appear as hyperdense, calcified areas within the mass.
On Contrast-Enhancement, only minimal to mild contrast enhancement is seen in the early arterial phase, followed by diffuse enhancement during the late venous phase.
Computed tomography angiography shows a nodular pattern of contrast enhancement in the early phase, attributable to small vessels within the lesion.

CVM shows hypointense or isointense signals on T1-weighted (T1W) MRI sequences and heterogeneous hyperintensity on T2-weighted (T2W) MRI, due to intervening areas of thrombosis devoid of hyperintensity.[12]
